instruction: Shmuel, verbatim, 2026-09-09: "I don't wanna see, like, repeating patterns all over." The Herodian ashlar is a 300 cm tile, so on a 60 m wall the same five stones appear 20 times in a grid; the Jerusalem paving is a 500 cm tile over the courts and the mount platform. The textures are accepted and are NOT re-authored: the repetition is broken in the material graph.
samplingModeNote: No UV warp. 15 Herodian Ashlar LAYOUT slices (1-D Wang edges per course, V5 bed joints) in Texture2DArrays; every 300 cm boundary carries 1 of 3 boundary-stone types, hashed per cell row; slice switches happen only at joints (analytic thresholds), boundary stones render from a diagonal slice where they wrap inside one texture. Implicit samplers, stock nodes, no Custom node. Built by Scripts/release_antirepeat_layouts.py.

statistics.why: every counter read back 0: -nullrhi builds no shader map, so instruction and sampler counts are not measurable in this process. The exact per-pixel texture fetch count in shaderCost.textureFetchesPerPixel is counted from the graph and is the honest cost figure here.
